quote: [repo content] Stale binary silently routes to Default — the fallback incident (2026-05-23).
statement: Interceptor/SKILL.md names a dated incident (2026-05-23): a rebuilt CLI binary that was never copied into place left an old binary silently unable to recognize the --context flag, so browser commands intended for the isolated test profile silently routed into the operator's own Default working window instead.
subject: self

quote: [repo content] Mitigation: the Preflight Isolation Gate (above) hard-fails on version mismatch with exit code 4
statement: Interceptor/SKILL.md ties the 2026-05-23 stale-binary incident to its mitigation: the Preflight Isolation Gate hard-fails with exit code 4 on any version below the minimum, and every workflow now runs the gate as its explicit first step, with recovery via Workflows/Update.md followed by killing and respawning the daemon.

quote: [repo content] RETIRED behavior — never re-derive it. The old "fall back to the first available / Default context..." rule is DELETED.
statement: Interceptor/SKILL.md marks the old 'fall back to the first available / Default context when the pinned context isn't found' rule as RETIRED and DELETED, replacing it with an unconditional hard stop on any missing or stale pinned context; the doctrine explicitly instructs never to re-derive the old fallback, framing it as a remembered failure mode that produced a durable rule change.
subject: self

quote: [repo content] Measured live 2026-07-30: over 5s with two real element resizes, the pinned test context reported visibilityState: hidden, 0 rAF ticks and 0 ResizeObserver callbacks
statement: Interceptor/SKILL.md reports a dated live measurement (2026-07-30) with the test context backgrounded: over 5s spanning two real element resizes, visibilityState was 'hidden' with zero rAF ticks and zero ResizeObserver callbacks while setInterval fired 5 times, cited as the basis for routing animation/viewport claims through Tools/VerifyViewport.ts rather than the standard test context.
subject: self

quote: [repo content] the tilde scrub was silently a no-op (fixed 2026-07-04)
statement: Interceptor/SKILL.md records that on bash 5.2+, Tools/Pin.sh's tilde-scrubbing substitution (${SRC/#$HOME/~}) silently became a no-op, causing PINNED_FROM.txt to ship an absolute home path and tripping Pin.sh's own leak-guard FATAL; the bug is dated fixed 2026-07-04 by rewriting the substitution as a quoted rel_home() helper.
subject: self

quote: [repo content] Two traps found live on the 0.22.37 upgrade (2026-07-28)
statement: Interceptor/SKILL.md dates a live operational occasion (2026-07-28) on which upgrading to daemon 0.22.37 surfaced two traps (a manifest symlinked into the source tree, a stale standalone daemon surviving pkill), both diagnosed using the pre-existing 'interceptor diagnose' command, documented as available since 0.22.2 — already-existing machinery exercised on a later, independent occasion.
subject: self

quote: [repo content] v0.13.3 renamed --os to --trusted (canonical). --os is kept as a deprecated alias and emits a warning.
statement: Interceptor/SKILL.md records that v0.13.3 renamed the --os flag to --trusted as canonical, keeping --os only as a deprecated alias that emits a warning, and instructs new code to lead with --trusted.
subject: self

quote: [repo content] compared against the upstream $INTERCEPTOR_SRC/extension/dist if present. Mismatch → fail with re-pin remediation. Upstream absent (currently true) → WARN and continue.
statement: Interceptor's built-from-source Chrome extension gets provenance recorded in Extension/PINNED_FROM.txt (source path, manifest version, SHA256, timestamp) by Tools/Pin.sh; the Preflight Isolation Gate compares this against upstream extension/dist when present and fails on mismatch, but only warns when upstream is absent (noted as currently true).
subject: self

quote: [repo content] Instead of calling `fabric -p pattern_name`, LifeOS executes patterns natively
statement: Fabric executes its 240+ patterns natively by reading each pattern's Patterns/<name>/system.md and applying it directly as a prompt, reserving the external fabric CLI for only two fallback cases (YouTube transcript extraction and URL-fetch fallback), and instructs appending a JSONL execution-log entry to a shared skills execution log after every workflow run.
subject: self

quote: [repo content] echo '{"ts":"'$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)'","skill":"Fabric"
statement: Multiple independently-read skills (Fabric, SuggestSkills, CreateSkill) each instruct appending a JSONL entry to the same shared path (~/.claude/LIFEOS/MEMORY/SKILLS/execution.jsonl) with ts/skill/workflow/status/duration_s fields after every run, a repeated self-logging convention whose populated log lives outside this scope.
subject: self

quote: [repo content] Native-first — code and tokens are the source of truth, Figma is not a dependency.
